prompt: Which of the following best describes supply for a good?

options.label: A
options.text: The quantity producers sell at one price during a given period

options.label: B
options.text: The productive resources firms retain after making the good

options.label: C
options.text: The revenue producers receive from the final unit they sell

options.label: D
options.text: Quantities offered for sale at different prices

options.label: E
options.text: The number of firms legally permitted to produce the good

explanation: Supply lists the quantities producers are willing and able to sell at each possible price.

prompt: The law of supply states that, other things constant,

options.label: A
options.text: Quantity supplied remains constant when the good's price changes

options.label: B
options.text: Supply decreases whenever production technology improves

options.label: C
options.text: Quantity supplied increases when the good's own price increases

options.label: D
options.text: Quantity supplied decreases when the good's own price increases

options.label: E
options.text: Supply increases whenever the number of sellers decreases

explanation: A higher price makes offering additional units more rewarding. With other factors constant, quantity supplied therefore increases.

prompt: If the price of a good increases, which of the following will most likely occur, ceteris paribus?

options.label: A
options.text: The supply of the good will shift to the left

options.label: B
options.text: The quantity supplied of the good will decrease

options.label: C
options.text: The quantity supplied of the good will increase

options.label: D
options.text: The quantity supplied of the good will remain unchanged

options.label: E
options.text: The supply of the good will shift to the right

explanation: A higher own-price encourages sellers to offer more units, moving up the existing supply curve.

prompt: Which of the following is a determinant that can shift the supply curve for a good?

options.label: A
options.text: The price-quantity combination selected on the curve

options.label: B
options.text: The good's current price, with other factors constant

options.label: C
options.text: The slope measured between two points on the curve

options.label: D
options.text: The price of an input used in production

options.label: E
options.text: The quantity currently shown on the supply curve

explanation: Input prices affect the cost of producing at every output price. Changing them shifts the supply curve.

prompt: An upward-sloping supply curve shows that

options.label: A
options.text: New technology is associated with movement along the curve

options.label: B
options.text: Lower input prices are associated with smaller quantities supplied

options.label: C
options.text: Higher prices are associated with larger quantities supplied

options.label: D
options.text: More sellers are associated with smaller market supply

options.label: E
options.text: Higher prices are associated with smaller quantities supplied

explanation: An upward-sloping supply curve pairs higher prices with larger quantities supplied, holding other supply determinants constant.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which labeled point represents the larger quantity supplied?

options.label: A
options.text: Point A, because it is associated with the lower price

options.label: B
options.text: Neither point, because both lie on the same supply curve

options.label: C
options.text: Point B, because it is associated with the higher price

options.label: D
options.text: Point A, because it lies closer to the quantity axis

options.label: E
options.text: Point B, because it represents a rightward supply shift

explanation: Point B has both a higher price and a larger quantity than A. This represents movement up the same supply curve.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. An upward-sloping curve labeled S contains point A at a low price and low quantity and point B at a higher price and larger quantity.

graphScenes.caption: Schematic; only labeled numbers are quantitative

prompt: A change in a good's own price causes

options.label: A
options.text: A leftward shift of its supply curve at every price

options.label: B
options.text: A rightward shift of its supply curve at every possible market price

options.label: C
options.text: A change in the technology used to produce the good

options.label: D
options.text: A movement from one point to another on its supply curve

options.label: E
options.text: A change in the number of sellers in its market

explanation: The good's own price selects a quantity on the existing supply curve. Changing it causes movement along that curve.

prompt: An increase in supply for a good means that producers

options.label: A
options.text: Sell more only because the good's current price has risen

options.label: B
options.text: Are willing to sell less at every possible price

options.label: C
options.text: Offer more for sale at every price

options.label: D
options.text: Face a smaller quantity range on the existing supply schedule

options.label: E
options.text: Move upward and rightward along the existing supply curve

explanation: An increase in supply means producers offer more at every price. The entire supply curve shifts right.

prompt: A decrease in supply for a good means that producers

options.label: A
options.text: Face a larger quantity range on the existing supply schedule

options.label: B
options.text: Offer less for sale at every price

options.label: C
options.text: Are willing to sell more at every possible price

options.label: D
options.text: Sell less only because the good's current price has fallen

options.label: E
options.text: Move downward and leftward along the existing supply curve

explanation: A decrease in supply means producers offer less at every price. The entire supply curve shifts left.

prompt: Based on the figure below, the change from point A to point B is best described as

options.label: A
options.text: An increase in supply caused by more sellers

options.label: B
options.text: A decrease in supply caused by higher input prices

options.label: C
options.text: An increase in supply caused by improved technology

options.label: D
options.text: A price-induced increase in quantity supplied

options.label: E
options.text: A decrease in quantity supplied caused by a higher price

explanation: A to B raises both price and quantity on S1. It therefore shows an increase in quantity supplied.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. An upward-sloping curve labeled S1 contains point A at price P1 and quantity Q1 and point B at higher price P2 and larger quantity Q2. An arrow points from A to B.

graphScenes.caption: Schematic; only labeled numbers are quantitative

prompt: If the price of an input used to produce a good increases, the good's supply will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease because producing each quantity becomes less attractive

options.label: B
options.text: Increase because quantity supplied rises along the same curve

options.label: C
options.text: Increase because producers can charge more for the input

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease because the good's own market price automatically falls

options.label: E
options.text: Remain unchanged because input prices are not on either axis

explanation: More expensive inputs make production more costly at each selling price. Producers supply fewer units, shifting supply left.

prompt: An improvement in production technology will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Increase quantity supplied by raising the good's current price

options.label: B
options.text: Increase supply by allowing more output from given resources

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease supply by requiring producers to charge higher prices

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease quantity supplied by lowering the good's current price

options.label: E
options.text: Leave supply unchanged because technology is not on either axis

explanation: Better technology allows more output from available inputs. Producers can offer more at every price, shifting supply right.

prompt: A per-unit government subsidy paid to sellers will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease supply because sellers receive less revenue per unit

options.label: B
options.text: Leave supply unchanged because the payment is not an input

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease quantity supplied only by lowering the market price

options.label: D
options.text: Increase quantity supplied only by raising the market price

options.label: E
options.text: Increase supply through a stronger per-unit incentive

explanation: A per-unit subsidy adds to sellers' receipts for each unit. It encourages more output at any given market price and shifts supply right.

prompt: A per-unit tax imposed on sellers will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Increase quantity supplied along the same supply curve

options.label: B
options.text: Increase supply because the tax raises sellers' net receipts

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease quantity supplied only after the market price falls

options.label: D
options.text: Leave supply unchanged because the tax is paid to government

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease supply through a weaker per-unit incentive

explanation: A per-unit tax reduces what sellers retain from each sale. They offer fewer units at each market price, shifting supply left.

prompt: An increase in the number of sellers in a market will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Leave market supply unchanged at each price

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease market supply at each price

options.label: C
options.text: Increase market supply at each price

options.label: D
options.text: Increase quantity supplied on one seller's curve

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease quantity supplied on one seller's curve

explanation: New sellers contribute additional quantities at each price. Their entry increases market supply.

prompt: If producers expect a storable good's price to rise next month, its current supply will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease as some units are withheld for future sale

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease only after the current price has fallen

options.label: C
options.text: Remain unchanged because the expected price is not current

options.label: D
options.text: Increase only after the current price has risen

options.label: E
options.text: Increase as all future production is sold immediately

explanation: If goods can be stored, sellers may hold them for the expected higher future price. Withholding goods reduces current supply.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which of the following could have caused the shift from S1 to S2?

options.label: A
options.text: A decrease in the number of firms selling the good

options.label: B
options.text: A decrease in the good's current market price

options.label: C
options.text: An increase in the price of an essential input

options.label: D
options.text: An expectation that the good's future price will rise

options.label: E
options.text: Improved production technology

explanation: The rightward shift to S2 means more is offered at every price. Improved technology can produce this increase in supply.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. Two upward-sloping curves are labeled S1 and S2, with S2 entirely to the right of S1. An arrow points from S1 toward S2.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which event is consistent with the shift shown for bread?

options.label: A
options.text: An increase in the number of bakeries in the market

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in the current market price of bread

options.label: C
options.text: An increase in the price of flour used by bakeries

options.label: D
options.text: An improvement in commercial baking technology

options.label: E
options.text: A decrease in the price of flour used by bakeries

explanation: More expensive flour raises the cost of making bread. Producers offer less at each bread price, shifting supply left.
graphDescription: Price per loaf is on the vertical axis and quantity of bread supplied is on the horizontal axis. Two upward-sloping curves are labeled S1 and S2, with S2 entirely to the left of S1. An arrow points from S1 toward S2.

prompt: The market supply curve for a good is found by

options.label: A
options.text: Adding individual quantities supplied at each price

options.label: B
options.text: Averaging individual quantities supplied at each price

options.label: C
options.text: Selecting the seller that offers the greatest quantity

options.label: D
options.text: Subtracting the smallest individual supply from the largest

options.label: E
options.text: Adding the prices each seller receives at each quantity

explanation: At a common price, add all sellers' quantities supplied. This horizontal sum gives market supply.

prompt: At a price of $9, Firm A supplies 4 units and Firm B supplies 7 units. If they are the only sellers, market quantity supplied is

options.label: A
options.text: 7 units

options.label: B
options.text: 3 units

options.label: C
options.text: 28 units

options.label: D
options.text: 4 units

options.label: E
options.text: 11 units

explanation: At the same price, the sellers' quantities add to 4 + 7 = 11 units.

prompt: Which of the following best explains why a higher output price can increase quantity supplied?

options.label: A
options.text: The higher price increases the number of sellers automatically in every market

options.label: B
options.text: The higher price reduces the prices sellers pay for all productive inputs

options.label: C
options.text: The higher price improves the production technology available to every seller

options.label: D
options.text: The higher price increases the reward sellers receive for offering additional units

options.label: E
options.text: The higher price reduces the quantities sellers are willing to offer at every price

explanation: A higher price increases the reward from selling another unit. Sellers respond by supplying more along the existing curve.

prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes supply from quantity supplied?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply changes only with own-price; quantity supplied changes only with technology

options.label: B
options.text: Supply applies only to markets; quantity supplied applies only to individual sellers

options.label: C
options.text: Supply is the full price-quantity relationship; quantity supplied is an amount at one price

options.label: D
options.text: Supply measures ability to sell; quantity supplied measures willingness without ability

options.label: E
options.text: Supply is an amount at one price; quantity supplied is the full price-quantity relationship

explanation: Supply describes quantities offered across all prices. Quantity supplied is the amount offered at one particular price.

prompt: A machine enables a factory to produce more units per worker-hour. This change primarily represents

options.label: A
options.text: A higher output price that increases quantity supplied

options.label: B
options.text: An expectation that future output prices will increase

options.label: C
options.text: A reduction in the number of sellers in the market

options.label: D
options.text: A technological improvement that increases supply

options.label: E
options.text: A lower output price that decreases quantity supplied

explanation: Producing more with the same worker time increases productivity. The factory can offer more at every price, increasing supply.

prompt: Based on the figure below, an increase in the good's price from P1 to P2 causes

options.label: A
options.text: Quantity supplied to decrease from Q2 to Q1

options.label: B
options.text: Supply to increase from S1 to S2

options.label: C
options.text: Quantity supplied to increase from Q1 to Q2

options.label: D
options.text: The number of sellers to increase automatically

options.label: E
options.text: Supply to decrease along the same curve

explanation: The rise from P1 to P2 increases quantity supplied from Q1 to Q2 on the same curve.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. An upward-sloping curve labeled S1 contains point A at price P1 and quantity Q1 and point B at higher price P2 and larger quantity Q2. Dashed guides connect both points to their labeled axis values.

graphScenes.caption: Schematic; only labeled numbers are quantitative

prompt: A decrease in the price of electricity used by a factory will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Increase quantity supplied only by raising the product's price

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease quantity supplied only by lowering the product's price

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease the factory's supply of its product

options.label: D
options.text: Increase the factory's supply of its product

options.label: E
options.text: Leave the factory's supply unchanged at every product price

explanation: Cheaper electricity lowers an input cost. Production becomes more attractive at each price, shifting supply right.

prompt: A decrease in a good's current market price, with all other factors unchanged, will

options.label: A
options.text: Leave quantity supplied unchanged on the existing curve

options.label: B
options.text: Reduce quantity supplied along the existing curve

options.label: C
options.text: Increase supply by shifting the curve to the right

options.label: D
options.text: Increase quantity supplied along the existing curve

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease supply by shifting the curve to the left

explanation: A lower selling price reduces the reward for offering additional units. Sellers reduce quantity supplied along the existing curve.

prompt: A drought that reduces crop yields will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Leave the crop supply schedule unchanged at every price

options.label: B
options.text: Increase the supply of crops at every market price

options.label: C
options.text: Increase quantity supplied only because crop prices rise

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease quantity supplied only because crop prices fall

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease the supply of crops at every market price

explanation: A drought reduces the crops farmers can produce. Less output is offered at each price, shifting crop supply left.

prompt: A regulation that raises the per-unit compliance expense of production will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Increase quantity supplied through a higher current price

options.label: B
options.text: Leave supply unchanged because the rule applies to every seller

options.label: C
options.text: Increase supply by increasing sellers' receipts from each unit

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease quantity supplied through a lower current price

options.label: E
options.text: Decrease supply by reducing the incentive to produce each unit

explanation: A per-unit compliance expense raises the cost of supplying each unit. Producers offer fewer units at a given selling price.

prompt: Why is a market supply curve generally upward-sloping?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher prices reduce the quantities all individual sellers offer

options.label: B
options.text: Higher prices encourage larger quantities offered

options.label: C
options.text: Lower prices increase the number of firms in every market

options.label: D
options.text: Lower prices reduce all input prices by the same proportion

options.label: E
options.text: Higher prices cause production technology to improve automatically

explanation: Higher prices encourage individual producers to supply more. Adding their quantities at each price gives an upward-sloping market supply curve.

prompt: A producer becomes willing to sell an additional unit only after the market price rises. This behavior is most consistent with

options.label: A
options.text: A decrease in supply caused by a lower expected future price

options.label: B
options.text: A leftward shift caused by an increase in input prices

options.label: C
options.text: A change in market supply caused by an additional seller

options.label: D
options.text: A rightward shift caused by an improvement in technology

options.label: E
options.text: The direct relationship between price and quantity supplied

explanation: A higher own-price strengthens the incentive to sell additional output. Quantity supplied increases along the existing curve.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which combination of events is represented by the movement from A to B and the shift from S1 to S2?

options.label: A
options.text: A decrease in the good's price, followed by an increase in an input price

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in an input price, followed by an increase in the good's price

options.label: C
options.text: An improvement in technology, followed by a decrease in the good's price

options.label: D
options.text: A decrease in the number of sellers, followed by a decrease in the good's price

options.label: E
options.text: An increase in the good’s price, followed by improved production technology

explanation: A to B raises the own-price and increases quantity supplied on S1. Improved technology then shifts supply right to S2.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. S1 and S2 slope upward, with S2 to the right of S1. Point A is low on S1, point B is higher and to the right on S1, and point C is directly right of B on S2 at the same price.

prompt: The price of a manufacturer's output rises while the price of an essential input falls. Which statement correctly describes the two effects?

options.label: A
options.text: Quantity supplied increases twice along the original supply curve

options.label: B
options.text: Supply shifts right; quantity supplied rises along it

options.label: C
options.text: Supply shifts left, and quantity supplied decreases along the new curve

options.label: D
options.text: Supply shifts right twice because both prices are supply determinants

options.label: E
options.text: Supply remains fixed because the two price changes necessarily offset

explanation: Cheaper inputs shift supply right. A higher output price also encourages more units through movement up the applicable supply curve.

prompt: An input price and the good's own price both increase. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply increases, while the own-price increase lowers quantity supplied along the new curve

options.label: B
options.text: Supply decreases twice because both prices are determinants of supply

options.label: C
options.text: Supply decreases, while the own-price increase raises quantity supplied along the new curve

options.label: D
options.text: The final quantity supplied must rise because the good's own price increased

options.label: E
options.text: Quantity supplied increases twice along the original supply curve

explanation: Higher input costs reduce supply, while the higher selling price encourages more output. The final quantity depends on the relative sizes of these opposing effects.

prompt: Farmers can use the same land to grow corn or soybeans. If the price of corn increases, which change is most likely in the soybean market?

options.label: A
options.text: The supply of soybeans increases as corn becomes more profitable

options.label: B
options.text: The quantity of soybeans supplied decreases because its own price rose

options.label: C
options.text: The quantity of soybeans supplied increases along its original curve

options.label: D
options.text: The supply of soybeans remains unchanged because only corn's price changed

options.label: E
options.text: The supply of soybeans decreases as land is shifted toward corn

explanation: Corn and soybeans compete for the same land. A higher corn price draws resources away from soybeans, decreasing soybean supply.

prompt: Based on the figure below, the shift in supply for Good X is most consistent with which event?

options.label: A
options.text: A per-unit subsidy paid to producers of Good X

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in the price of an input used for Good X

options.label: C
options.text: A per-unit tax imposed on producers of Good X

options.label: D
options.text: An increase in the current market price of Good X

options.label: E
options.text: A decrease in the number of producers of Good X

explanation: A per-unit subsidy raises sellers' receipts at each market price. This encourages more supply of X and shifts the curve right.
graphDescription: Price of Good X is on the vertical axis and quantity of Good X supplied is on the horizontal axis. Two upward-sloping curves are labeled S1 and S2, with S2 to the right of S1. A rightward arrow connects the curves.

prompt: Several new firms enter a market while the good's own price remains unchanged. Which of the following will most likely occur?

options.label: A
options.text: Quantity supplied will decrease along every entrant's original curve

options.label: B
options.text: Market supply will decrease because each incumbent must offer fewer units

options.label: C
options.text: Market supply will remain unchanged because the market price did not change

options.label: D
options.text: More sellers increase the quantities offered at each price

options.label: E
options.text: Quantity supplied will increase along every incumbent's original curve

explanation: Market supply adds all sellers' quantities at each price. Entrants add output to this sum and increase market supply.

prompt: A $3 per-unit tax is imposed on sellers of a product. Holding other factors constant, sellers will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Offer the same units at each price because all sellers face the tax

options.label: B
options.text: Sellers offer fewer units at each price because net returns fall

options.label: C
options.text: Offer more units at each market price because the posted price is unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: Move downward along the original supply curve because the tax lowers price

options.label: E
options.text: Move upward along the original supply curve because the tax raises price

explanation: A per-unit tax reduces sellers' net receipts. It discourages output at each market price, shifting supply left.

prompt: Production technology improves at the same time that sellers receive a new per-unit subsidy. What happens to supply?

options.label: A
options.text: Quantity supplied increases only through movement along the original curve

options.label: B
options.text: Quantity supplied decreases only through movement along the original curve

options.label: C
options.text: Supply increases; both changes encourage production

options.label: D
options.text: Supply remains unchanged because the two changes necessarily offset

options.label: E
options.text: Supply decreases because both changes reduce the return from production

explanation: Better technology raises productivity, and a subsidy raises sellers' receipts. Both encourage more output at each price and increase supply.

prompt: Based on the figure below, what does the horizontal distance between S1 and S2 at price P represent?

options.label: A
options.text: Additional quantity supplied at the same price

options.label: B
options.text: The decrease in quantity supplied after production technology improves

options.label: C
options.text: The increase in quantity supplied caused by a higher own-price

options.label: D
options.text: The decrease in market supply after the number of sellers rises

options.label: E
options.text: The increase in supply caused only by a change in the good's price

explanation: At P, S2 offers more units than S1. Their horizontal gap measures the increase in supply at that price.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. S1 and S2 slope upward but are not parallel, with S2 to the right. A horizontal line at price P intersects S1 at Q1 and S2 at the larger quantity Q2; the interval from Q1 to Q2 is highlighted.

prompt: At a price of $8, three firms supply 2, 5, and 6 units, respectively. At a price of $12, they supply 4, 7, and 9 units. Which pair gives market quantity supplied at the two prices?

options.text: 11 units at $8 and 18 units at $12

options.label: B
options.text: 15 units at $8 and 22 units at $12

options.label: D
options.text: 13 units at $8 and 20 units at $12

options.label: E
options.text: 9 units at $8 and 16 units at $12

explanation: At $8, quantities add to 2 + 5 + 6 = 13. At $12, they add to 4 + 7 + 9 = 20 units.

prompt: At a price of $15, market quantity supplied is 27 units. If two sellers supply 8 and 11 units, how many units does the third seller supply?

options.label: A
options.text: 6 units

options.label: B
options.text: 8 units

options.text: 19 units

options.label: D
options.text: 9 units

options.label: E
options.text: 16 units

prompt: At every price, a new seller offers 4 units of a good. If all original sellers' offers remain unchanged, market supply will

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease by 4 units at each price

options.label: B
options.text: Increase by 4 units at each price

options.label: C
options.text: Remain unchanged because individual supply is unchanged

options.label: D
options.text: Increase by 4 percent at each price

options.label: E
options.text: Increase only when the good's price rises

explanation: The entrant adds 4 units at each price to the existing sellers' output. Market supply increases by 4 units at every price.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which relationship among the curves is correct?

prompt: A workshop can use the same machine-hours to make desks or cabinets. If the price of cabinets rises, the supply of desks will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Remain unchanged because cabinet prices are not shown on the desk graph

options.label: B
options.text: Increase because higher cabinet prices make all woodworking more profitable

options.text: Decrease because the current market price of desks must also fall

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease because producing cabinets now has a greater opportunity cost

options.label: E
options.text: Increase through movement upward along the original desk supply curve

prompt: A licensing rule adds a required fee for every unit a seller produces. Holding the product's price constant, the rule will most likely

options.label: A
options.text: Raise the quantity sellers offer because licensing certifies every unit

options.label: B
options.text: Reduce quantity offered through a weaker incentive

options.label: C
options.text: Leave the quantity offered unchanged because the rule is legally required

options.label: D
options.text: Cause movement downward along the original curve without changing supply

options.label: E
options.text: Cause movement upward along the original curve without changing supply

explanation: The required per-unit fee reduces the seller's net return. Sellers offer fewer units at each price, decreasing supply.

prompt: Producers of a storable crop come to expect a much higher selling price next season. Which current response is most consistent with this expectation?

options.label: A
options.text: They withhold some current output, decreasing current supply

options.label: B
options.text: They release more current output, increasing current supply

options.label: C
options.text: They leave current supply unchanged because storage is possible

options.label: D
options.text: They move downward along the current supply curve at every price

options.label: E
options.text: They move upward along the current supply curve at every price

prompt: Supply of a product will unambiguously increase if the number of sellers rises and

options.label: A
options.text: A per-unit tax on production increases

options.label: B
options.text: Producers expect a higher future price

options.label: C
options.text: The price of an essential input decreases

options.label: D
options.text: Production technology becomes less effective

options.label: E
options.text: The price of an essential input increases

explanation: Seller entry adds output, and cheaper inputs encourage existing sellers to produce more. Both changes increase market supply.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which statement best explains why supply moved from S1 to S2 despite an increase in the good's current price?

options.label: A
options.text: Price causes movement; another determinant shifts supply

options.label: B
options.text: Improved technology reduced supply by more than the price increase raised it

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: The price increase reduced both supply and quantity supplied by equal amounts

options.label: E

prompt: The price of a product falls at the same time production technology improves. Which statement correctly describes the two effects?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply shifts left twice because both changes reduce seller receipts

options.label: B
options.text: Quantity supplied must increase because technology always dominates price

options.label: C
options.text: Supply shifts right twice because both changes increase production

options.label: D
options.text: Quantity supplied moves down a curve, while the supply curve shifts right

options.label: E
options.text: Quantity supplied moves up a curve, while the supply curve shifts left

explanation: The lower own-price reduces quantity supplied, while better technology increases supply. Their opposing effects make the final quantity change uncertain.

prompt: A new production method raises productivity while the price of a required raw material rises. What can be concluded about supply?

options.label: A
options.text: Indeterminate; the determinants exert opposing effects

options.label: B
options.text: Quantity supplied moves along one curve because neither change affects supply

options.label: C
options.text: Supply remains unchanged because the changes necessarily have equal effects

options.label: D
options.text: Supply must decrease because input prices are always the stronger determinant

options.label: E
options.text: Supply must increase because technology is always the stronger determinant

explanation: Improved technology increases supply, but more expensive raw materials decrease it. Their relative sizes determine the net shift.

prompt: A product's current price decreases while its production technology improves. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply shifts right, while quantity supplied moves downward along the new curve

options.label: B
options.text: The two changes necessarily leave the final quantity supplied unchanged

options.label: C
options.text: Supply shifts left, while quantity supplied moves upward along the new curve

options.label: D
options.text: Both changes decrease quantity supplied along the original curve

options.label: E
options.text: Both changes increase supply because both strengthen seller incentives

explanation: Better technology shifts supply right. The lower own-price then selects a smaller quantity on that new curve than a higher price would.

prompt: Sellers of a storable good expect its price to fall next month. Which current response is most likely?

options.label: A
options.text: Current supply increases as sellers move planned future sales into the present

options.label: B
options.text: Current supply decreases as sellers move present sales into the future

options.label: C
options.text: Current quantity supplied falls only through movement along the original curve

options.label: D
options.text: Current quantity supplied rises only after the current market price increases along the original curve

options.label: E
options.text: Current supply remains fixed because expectations concern a future price

explanation: Expected lower future prices make selling now more attractive than waiting. Producers release more current output, shifting supply right.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which sequence is represented by the change from A to B and then from B to C?

options.label: A
options.text: A decrease in the good's own price followed by improved technology that shifts supply right

options.label: B
options.text: An increase in supply followed by a decrease in the good's own price

options.label: C
options.text: A decrease in supply followed by a decrease in the good's own price

options.label: D
options.text: An increase in the good's own price followed by an increase in an input price

options.label: E
options.text: An increase in the number of sellers followed by a higher input price

explanation: A to B raises price and quantity on S1. B to C then shifts supply left at that price, as higher input costs could do.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. S2 lies to the left of S1. Point A is low on S1, point B is directly above and to the right on S1 at a higher price, and point C is directly left of B on S2 at the same higher price.

prompt: Which of the following best explains why a seller may offer a second unit only at a higher price than the first?

options.label: A
options.text: The seller becomes an additional firm when the second unit is produced

options.label: B
options.text: The higher price makes the additional use of limited productive resources worthwhile

options.label: C
options.text: The second unit automatically improves the technology used for all output

options.label: D
options.text: The first unit creates a legal requirement to supply a second unit

options.label: E
options.text: The second unit shifts the seller's entire supply curve farther to the right

explanation: Additional production can require resources with increasingly valuable alternative uses. A higher selling price can compensate sellers for redirecting those resources.

prompt: Favorable weather raises output per acre for orange growers. Holding orange prices constant, which change will most likely occur?

options.label: A
options.text: Orange supply shifts right because growers can offer more at each price

options.label: B
options.text: Orange supply remains unchanged because the number of acres did not change

options.label: C
options.text: Orange supply shifts left because each acre now produces more fruit

options.label: D
options.text: Orange quantity supplied falls only through movement along the original curve

options.label: E
options.text: Orange quantity supplied rises only through movement along the original curve

explanation: A higher yield produces more oranges from the same land. Growers can supply more at each price.

prompt: One firm leaves a market while every remaining firm's supply schedule is unchanged. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Market quantity supplied increases along the original market curve at each price

options.label: B
options.text: Every remaining firm's quantity supplied decreases at each unchanged price

options.label: C
options.text: Market supply decreases even though the remaining individual supply curves do not shift

options.label: D
options.text: Each remaining firm's supply shifts right to replace the departing firm automatically

options.label: E
options.text: Market supply remains unchanged at every possible price because no remaining firm's supply curve shifts

explanation: Each seller contributes to market supply at every price. Removing one seller reduces the market total even if the others' curves do not change.

prompt: At a price of $6, three sellers supply 5, 7, and 9 units. One seller's quantity rises from 7 to 11 units at that price. What happens to market quantity supplied?

options.label: A

options.text: It decreases from 21 units to 17 units

options.text: It increases from 16 units to 20 units

options.label: D
options.text: It increases from 21 units to 32 units

options.text: It increases from 21 units to 25 units

explanation: Initial supply totals 5 + 7 + 9 = 21 units. Replacing 7 with 11 adds 4, giving 25 units.

options.text: 11 units

prompt: An essential input becomes cheaper, but several sellers leave the market. Which conclusion about market supply is valid?

options.label: A
options.text: Market supply must decrease because the number of sellers determines all supply

options.label: B
options.text: Market supply must increase at every possible price because input prices determine every seller's supply response

options.label: C
options.text: The direction of the change is indeterminate because the two events have opposing effects

options.label: D
options.text: Market supply remains unchanged because the events necessarily offset exactly

options.label: E
options.text: Quantity supplied moves along one market curve because both events change price

explanation: Cheaper inputs encourage greater supply, but seller exit removes output. The sizes of these changes determine the net shift.

prompt: A seller supplies zero units at $4, two units at $7, and five units at $10. Which observation is supported?

options.label: A
options.text: The schedule shows supply decreasing as the product's own price rises

options.label: B
options.text: The schedule shows that additional sellers entered between each price

options.label: C
options.text: The schedule proves that production technology improved at higher prices

options.label: D
options.text: The schedule shows the seller's supply curve shifting right at each price

options.label: E
options.text: A direct relationship between price and quantity supplied

explanation: The schedule offers more units at higher own-prices. This positive price-quantity relationship illustrates the law of supply.

prompt: A product's price and quantity supplied both rise between two months. Why does this observation not by itself prove the law of supply caused the change?

options.label: A
options.text: The law of supply requires price and quantity supplied to move oppositely

options.label: B
options.text: The law of supply applies only when the number of firms changes between months

options.label: C
options.text: A higher price always shifts supply right rather than causing movement along it

options.label: D
options.text: A supply determinant may also have shifted the curve between the observations

options.label: E
options.text: Market supply is found by vertically adding individual prices at each quantity

explanation: The law of supply holds other determinants constant. Changes in inputs, technology, expectations, or seller numbers can shift supply between the observations.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which conclusion is valid?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply increased only at P1 because the two curves are not parallel

options.text: Quantity supplied remained unchanged because both curves slope upward

options.text: Supply rises at both prices, not necessarily equally

prompt: A factory can produce either bicycles or scooters with the same equipment. If the selling price of scooters rises, which effect on bicycle supply is most likely?

options.label: B
options.text: Bicycle supply decreases because equipment is redirected toward scooters

options.label: C
options.text: Bicycle supply remains unchanged because scooter prices are in another market

options.label: D
options.text: Bicycle supply increases because both products use the same equipment

options.label: E
options.text: Bicycle quantity supplied decreases because its own price must have fallen

explanation: A higher scooter price encourages firms to use shared equipment for scooters. Fewer resources remain for bicycles, reducing bicycle supply.

prompt: A required labor input becomes more expensive at the same time a per-unit production tax is imposed. What happens to supply?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply decreases because both changes weaken the incentive to produce at each price

options.label: B
options.text: Quantity supplied increases through movement along the original supply curve

options.label: C
options.text: Supply increases because both changes raise the amount sellers receive per unit

options.label: D
options.text: Quantity supplied decreases only if the good's current price also decreases

options.label: E
options.text: Supply remains unchanged because the changes necessarily offset each other

explanation: Higher labor costs and a per-unit tax both reduce the return from production at a given price. Both shift supply left.

prompt: A supply schedule shows larger quantities offered at every listed price after a new production process is adopted. Which conclusion is supported?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply remained unchanged because the listed prices did not change

options.label: B
options.text: Quantity supplied increased because the good's own price rose at every point

options.label: C
options.text: Quantity supplied decreased through movement down the original schedule

options.label: D
options.text: Supply decreased because the original quantities were smaller at each price

options.label: E
options.text: Supply increased because the entire price-quantity relationship shifted right

explanation: Offering more at every unchanged price indicates increased supply. A more productive production process shifts the curve right.

prompt: A manufacturer installs automation that reduces the time needed to produce each unit. Which change is most likely?

options.label: A
options.text: The manufacturer's quantity supplied falls along its original supply curve

options.label: B
options.text: Higher productivity increases the manufacturer’s supply

options.label: C
options.text: The manufacturer's supply decreases because fewer worker-hours are used per unit

options.label: D
options.text: The manufacturer's supply remains unchanged because the factory size is fixed

options.label: E
options.text: The manufacturer's quantity supplied rises only if the product's price increases

explanation: Automation reduces the time needed to produce each unit. Producers can offer more output at each selling price.

prompt: Two firms use different technologies and face different production constraints. Why may their individual supply schedules differ?

prompt: At a price of $10, four sellers supply 3, 5, 7, and 9 units. The seller supplying 9 units exits, while each remaining seller increases its quantity by 2 units at that price. What is the new market quantity supplied?

options.text: 21 units

options.label: D

prompt: Current supply of a storable good is affected by a decrease in an input price, entry of new sellers, and an expected increase in the good's future price. Which conclusion is valid?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: The net change in current supply is indeterminate because the determinants work in opposing directions

options.text: Current supply must decrease because expectations always outweigh current production incentives

prompt: At every listed price, a new technology adds 8 units to market supply, while the exit of two sellers removes a combined 11 units. Which change occurs in market supply?

options.text: It increases by 19 units at each listed price

options.text: It is indeterminate because both events change supply

options.label: E
options.text: It decreases by 19 units at each listed price

explanation: Technology adds 8 units and seller exit removes 11 at each price. Net supply decreases by 11 - 8 = 3 units at each price.

prompt: At a price of $11, three sellers supply 4, 6, and 8 units. A new seller supplies 5 units, while the original sellers change their quantities by +2, -1, and +3 units. What is the new market quantity supplied?

options.text: 22 units

options.label: D
options.text: 25 units

options.label: E
options.text: 27 units

prompt: At a price of $14, market quantity supplied is 28 units. Seller A supplies 10 units, and Seller B supplies twice as many units as Seller C. How many units does Seller B supply?

prompt: A farm can use the same field for wheat or barley. The price of wheat rises while the price of barley is unchanged. Which pair of effects is most likely?

prompt: Producers expect a good's price to rise next month. Which information is needed to predict the effect on current supply?

prompt: A good's price falls while an unrelated change shifts its supply curve left. What can be concluded about the final quantity supplied compared with the initial quantity?

prompt: Researchers observe that a good's price and quantity supplied both increased between two months. Why does this observation not prove movement along a single supply curve?

options.text: Compare point A with point D because both lie on upward-sloping supply curves

options.label: E
options.text: Compare point A on S1 with point C on S2 at the same price P1

explanation: A and C have the same price P1 on different supply curves. Their horizontal difference isolates the change in supply.

prompt: At a price of $7, three sellers initially supply 6, 7, and 8 units. A change in incentives raises the first seller's quantity by 4 units and lowers the other two quantities by 1 and 3 units. What happens to market quantity supplied?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases to 29 units because all absolute changes are added

options.label: B
options.text: It decreases to 17 units because the other sellers remove 4 units

options.label: C
options.text: It remains at 21 units because the individual changes sum to zero

options.label: D
options.text: It increases to 25 units because the first seller adds 4 units

options.label: E
options.text: It becomes indeterminate because individual sellers respond differently

explanation: Initial supply is 6 + 7 + 8 = 21 units. Individual changes total +4 - 1 - 3 = 0, so market quantity remains 21.

prompt: At price P1, Sellers A and B supply a total of 8 units. At higher price P2, market quantity supplied is 22 units, and Seller A supplies 9 units. Seller B's quantity at P2 is

options.label: A
options.text: 11 units

options.label: B
options.text: 9 units

options.label: C
options.text: 17 units

options.label: D
options.text: 14 units

options.label: E
options.text: 13 units

explanation: At P2, subtract A's 9 units from the market's 22. Seller B supplies 13 units.

prompt: Four one-unit sellers require minimum prices of $4, $7, $9, and $14. If the market price falls from $12 to $9, market quantity supplied becomes

options.label: A
options.text: 3 units

options.label: B
options.text: 2 units

options.label: C
options.text: 4 units

options.label: D
options.text: 1 unit

options.label: E
options.text: 9 units

explanation: At $9, units requiring minimum prices of $4, $7, and $9 can be supplied. The $14 unit cannot, giving a total of 3 units.

prompt: A new rule raises the per-unit expense of production at the same time the good's own price rises. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Both changes create movement upward along the original supply curve

options.label: B
options.text: Final quantity supplied must rise because own-price always dominates regulation

options.label: C
options.text: Supply shifts left, while the higher own-price raises quantity supplied along the new curve

options.label: D
options.text: Supply shifts right, while the higher own-price lowers quantity supplied along the new curve

options.label: E
options.text: Both changes shift supply left because each raises a price faced by sellers

explanation: The per-unit expense shifts supply left. The higher own-price encourages more output along the new curve, so final quantity depends on which effect is larger.

prompt: For a storable good, an input becomes cheaper and producers expect the good's future price to rise. Which conclusion about current supply is valid?

options.label: A
options.text: Current supply must decrease because both changes encourage producers to withhold output

options.label: B
options.text: Current supply must increase at every current price because both changes make present production and sales more profitable

options.label: C
options.text: Current supply remains unchanged because the two changes necessarily offset exactly

options.label: D
options.text: The net change is indeterminate because cheaper production raises supply while expected appreciation reduces it

options.label: E
options.text: Current quantity supplied changes only through movement along the original curve

explanation: Cheaper inputs increase current supply, while expected higher future prices encourage withholding. Their relative sizes determine the net change.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which event sequence is consistent with the movement from A to B and then B to C?

options.label: A
options.text: A higher input price shifts supply right, and then a higher own-price lowers quantity supplied

options.label: B
options.text: Quantity supplied rises on S1, and then the own-price change shifts the entire supply curve to S2

options.label: C
options.text: Seller exit increases supply at P1, and then a subsidy causes movement along S2

options.label: D
options.text: Supply decreases at price P1, and then a lower own-price raises quantity supplied on S2

options.label: E
options.text: Production technology improves at price P1, and then a higher own-price raises quantity supplied on S2

explanation: A to B increases supply at P1, consistent with improved technology. B to C raises price on S2 and increases quantity supplied.
graphDescription: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity supplied is on the horizontal axis. S2 lies to the right of S1. Point A is on S1 at price P1, point B is directly right of A on S2 at P1, and point C is above and to the right of B on S2.

prompt: The price of an essential input rises at the same time producers receive a new per-unit subsidy. Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Supply must increase at every market price because a subsidy always exceeds any increase in the price of an essential input

options.label: B
options.text: Quantity supplied moves along one curve because both changes affect producer revenue

options.label: C
options.text: The net supply shift depends on whether the subsidy or input-price increase has the larger effect

options.label: D
options.text: Supply must decrease because an input price always exceeds any subsidy

options.label: E
options.text: Supply remains unchanged because the two incentives offset by definition

explanation: Higher input costs decrease supply, while the subsidy increases it. Without their sizes, the net shift cannot be determined.

prompt: The price of Good Y rises, and producers can make either Good X or Good Y with the same resources. The price of Good X also rises. Which conclusion about Good X is supported?

options.label: A
options.text: Good X supply shifts left twice because both output prices increased

options.label: B
options.text: Good X supply shifts left, while its higher own-price raises quantity supplied along the new curve

options.label: C
options.text: Good X's final quantity supplied must fall because Good Y's price changed first

options.label: D
options.text: Good X supply shifts right, while its higher own-price lowers quantity supplied along the new curve

options.label: E
options.text: Good X quantity supplied rises twice along its original supply curve

explanation: Y's higher price draws shared resources away from X, decreasing X's supply. X's higher own-price encourages more output, leaving the final quantity uncertain.

prompt: Which combination of changes will unambiguously decrease current supply of a storable good?

options.label: A
options.text: Input prices rise, sellers enter, and production technology improves

options.label: B
options.text: Input prices rise, sellers enter, and producers expect the future price to fall

options.label: C
options.text: Input prices fall, several sellers leave, and producers expect the good's future price to rise substantially

options.label: D
options.text: Input prices fall, sellers enter, and production technology improves

options.label: E
options.text: Input prices rise, sellers leave, and producers expect the good's future price to rise

explanation: Higher input costs discourage production, seller exit removes output, and expected higher future prices encourage withholding. All three reduce current supply.

prompt: At a price of $9, four sellers supply 5, 7, 8, and 10 units. The seller supplying 10 units exits, and each remaining seller increases quantity supplied by 1 unit. Market quantity supplied changes by

options.label: A
options.text: A decrease of 3 units

options.label: B
options.text: An increase of 3 units

options.label: C
options.text: A decrease of 7 units

options.label: D
options.text: A decrease of 10 units

options.label: E
options.text: An increase of 7 units

explanation: Seller exit removes 10 from the initial 30 units. The remaining three sellers add 1 each, giving 23 units, a net decrease of 7.

prompt: Based on the figure below, which statement correctly distinguishes the two changes?

options.label: A
options.text: A to B is a supply increase, while B to C is a quantity-supplied decrease

options.label: B
options.text: A to B and B to C are both movements caused by changes in the good's own price

options.label: C
options.text: A to B and B to C are both supply shifts caused by changing determinants

options.label: D
options.text: A to B is an increase in quantity supplied, while B to C is an increase in supply

options.label: E
options.text: A to B is a quantity-supplied decrease, while B to C is a supply decrease

explanation: A to B raises price and quantity on S1. B to C moves right between supply curves at the same price, showing increased supply.

prompt: At price P1, four sellers supply 3, 5, 4, and 2 units. The fourth seller exits; the others change their quantities by +2, -1, and +3 units; then a new seller supplies 4 units. What is final market quantity supplied?

options.label: A
options.text: 20 units

options.label: B
options.text: 22 units

options.label: C
options.text: 16 units

options.label: D
options.text: 14 units

options.label: E
options.text: 18 units

explanation: Removing the fourth seller leaves 12 units. The others add a net 4 and the entrant adds 4, giving 20 units.

prompt: After several sellers enter and others leave a market, the total quantity supplied at every listed price is unchanged. Which conclusion is supported?

options.label: A
options.text: Every individual supply curve must be unchanged because market totals are unchanged

options.label: B
options.text: The good's own price must have changed by the same amount at every listed quantity

options.label: C
options.text: The entering and exiting sellers must offer identical quantities at every price

options.label: D
options.text: Market supply is unchanged even though the composition and individual supply schedules may have changed

options.label: E
options.text: Market supply shifted right and then moved left along the new supply curve

explanation: Market supply depends on the total offered at each price. Different individual sellers can produce the same totals, leaving the aggregate curve unchanged.
